```{r, message = FALSE}
# Question 1

# START OF FUNCTION 
#######################################################################
log_growth <- function(N0 = 5, r = .1, K = 100, tfinal = 100, tstep = 5){

#######################################################
# FUNCTION: log_growth
# PURPOSE: runs a logistic growth model
# INPUTS: initial population size (N0), growth rate(r), carrying capacity (K), end time for time vector (tfinal), timestep for time vector (tstep)
# OUT: dataframe with population size and time

times <- seq(from = 0, to = tfinal, by = tstep)

logdf <- data.frame(times, popsize = NA)

for (t in 1:length(times)){
    time <- logdf$times[t]
n <- (K/
    (1+
    ((K-N0)/N0)*exp((-r)*time)))
logdf$popsize[t] = n
}

return(logdf)
}
########################################################################
# END FUNCTION
log_results <- log_growth()

log_growth()

# Question 2

# START OF FUNCTION 
#######################################################################
plot_growth <- function(logdf = log_results){
library(tidyverse)
#######################################################
# FUNCTION: plot_growth
# PURPOSE: Takes log_growth dataframe and creates plot of population size over time
# INPUTS: dataframe from log_growth
# OUT: dataframe with population size and time

ggplot(
        data = logdf,
        mapping = aes(
            x = times,
            y = popsize
        )
    ) + geom_point() + geom_line() + xlab("Times") + ylab("Population Size")

}

########################################################################
# END FUNCTION

plot_growth()

```
